topics.title: Planning an investigation: variables, hypotheses, risk, apparatus, tables and diagrams

cards.front: What equation gives personal power from work done?
cards.back: Power = work done ÷ time; work done = weight × vertical height climbed.

cards.front: What is a controlled variable?
cards.back: One kept the same, so only the independent variable affects the result.

cards.front: Does repeating and averaging improve accuracy or reliability?
cards.back: Reliability: repeats that agree can be trusted.

cards.front: How is a results-table heading written?
cards.back: Quantity / unit, such as Time / s, with numbers only in the cells.

cards.front: State the Principle of Moments.
cards.back: In equilibrium, clockwise moments about a pivot equal anticlockwise moments.

cards.front: Give a unit for a moment.
cards.back: N m or N cm: force times distance.

cards.front: What must an apparatus diagram be to earn its marks?
cards.back: Two-dimensional, assembled, with open paths, and every piece labelled.

cards.front: How is the volume of an irregular solid found?
cards.back: By displacement: the rise in water level in a measuring cylinder.

topics.title: Carrying out an experiment: using apparatus correctly, skilfully and safely

cards.front: Where do you read a measuring cylinder?
cards.back: At eye level, at the bottom of the meniscus.

cards.front: Why is ethanol never warmed over a flame?
cards.back: Ethanol is flammable, so a flame could set it alight.

cards.front: Give the flame colours of lithium, sodium and potassium ions.
cards.back: Lithium crimson, sodium yellow-orange, potassium lilac.

cards.front: What are the tests for hydrogen and oxygen?
cards.back: Hydrogen: a lighted splint gives a squeaky pop. Oxygen: a glowing splint relights.

cards.front: Why can hydrogen be collected over water?
cards.back: It is insoluble in water, so it pushes the water out of the jar.

cards.front: Is 'exothermic' an observation?
cards.back: No, it is a deduction: write 'heat given out' or 'gets warmer'.

cards.front: How is the energy in food per gram worked out?
cards.back: Rise in temperature × volume of water × 4.2 ÷ mass of food.

cards.front: Which solution turns milky when carbon dioxide bubbles through it?
cards.back: Limewater, which starts colourless and turns milky.

topics.title: Analysing experimental data: accuracy, reliability, validity, anomalies and graphs

cards.front: What is an anomalous result?
cards.back: A reading that does not fit the pattern of the others.

cards.front: What is the extension of a spring?
cards.back: Its stretched length minus its unstretched length.

cards.front: How is a rate found from a time?
cards.back: Rate = 1 ÷ time, in s⁻¹.

cards.front: What is the unit of a gradient?
cards.back: The y-axis unit per the x-axis unit.
keyWords: y-axis unit per the x-axis unit

cards.front: Where is the total volume of gas read?
cards.back: From the level part of the curve, never by adding readings.

cards.front: What does the gradient of force against extension give?
cards.back: The spring constant, k, in N/cm.

cards.front: Which line goes through the points of a Physics graph?
cards.back: One straight line or smooth curve of best fit.

cards.front: What must an axis label contain?
cards.back: The quantity and its unit, as in the column heading.

topics.title: Drawing conclusions: evidence, proportionality, calculations and evaluation

cards.front: What must a conclusion quote besides the pattern?
cards.back: Numbers from the results, then the scientific reason.

cards.front: What graph shows direct proportion?
cards.back: A straight line through the origin.

cards.front: What graph shows y inversely proportional to x?
cards.back: A straight line through the origin of y against 1 ÷ x.

cards.front: How is a percentage change in mass worked out?
cards.back: Change in mass ÷ initial mass × 100, with its sign.

cards.front: How is x found for a hydrated salt?
cards.back: Moles of water ÷ moles of anhydrous salt.

cards.front: What do repeats and a mean improve?
cards.back: Reliability, not accuracy.

cards.front: What is heating to constant mass?
cards.back: Heating, cooling and weighing until two weighings agree.

cards.front: What is the answer for a claim about an untested condition?
cards.back: Cannot tell.
